thesis: The speakers argue that shame in men often stems from culturally limited roles and narrow definitions of how one can fulfill them, such as the expectation that provision must be achieved solely through money or protection. They further suggest that this shame is compounded when men provide in different ways, like sharing time or taking adventures, which go unacknowledged by a culture programmed to expect specific male ideals.
